title: Quantifying the impact of just-in-time (JIT) systems on freight rates
core_idea: Evaluate how JIT arrival policies — through lower average sailing speeds and reduced port waiting times — affect capesize freight rates by building a random forest model with capesize freight rate as the dependent variable, sailing speed and a port congestion index as main predictors, and supply/demand control variables, then conducting scenario analysis for varying JIT-driven speed and congestion levels.
tldr: The study aims to quantify the economic impact of maritime JIT systems on freight rates by modeling the combined effects of sailing speed and port congestion on capesize freight rates using a random forest and scenario analysis.
